title: Arizona Voters Are Worried About Water
summary:
In Arizona, many voters have a new top worry before this fall's midterm elections. It is water.

Arizona is in a long drought. That means it has had much less rain than usual for a long time. Canals carry water to the desert city of Phoenix, but that water is getting harder to come by. This summer, the federal government made deep cuts to the Colorado River water that Arizona cities get.

A recent survey from a group called the Center for the Future of Arizona found that, for the first time, water is voters' top concern.

Candidates now get more questions about how they will protect the state's water. Democrat Amish Shah, who is running for a U.S. House seat, said Arizona should save water and stop using it for data centers. His Republican opponent, Jay Feely, said the economy is still the top issue, but water is a big concern too.

One analysis found that farming uses about 75 percent of Arizona's water. Data centers use only a small share.
why_it_matters: Everyone needs water to drink, wash and grow food, so how leaders protect it affects kids and families every day.
